question.text: <math> <mrow> <mtext>0</mtext><mtext>.4</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>g</mtext></mrow> </math> of an organic compound on Kjeldahl’s analysis gave enough ammonia to just neutralize <math> <mrow> <mtext>20</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>ml</mtext></mrow> </math> of <math> <mrow> <mtext>1N</mtext><mtext> </mtext><msub> <mtext>H</mtext> <mtext>2</mtext> </msub> <msub> <mrow> <mtext>SO</mtext></mrow> <mtext>4</mtext> </msub> </mrow> </math> . What is the percentage of nitrogen in the compound?

solution.text:
milli equivalents of NH 3 = milli equivalents of H 2 SO 4
milli moles of NH 3 ×1=1 N×20 ml
milli moles of NH 3  = 20 milli moles
∴ mass of N= 2 0 ×14 100 0
=0.28
∴ % of N= 0.28 0.4 ×100=70%
